name: Assamite Institutions of the Third Crusade (Dark Ages)

text.content:
Source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book Two ("Saracens").

In the nights of the Third Crusade, the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} clan's Dark Ages hierarchy centers on four offices at the mountain fortress of Alamut, distinct from (and centuries earlier than) the modern-nights Schism figures known from Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite}.

The Eldest: The clan's supreme leader, called the Old Man by outsiders, is traditionally the oldest fourth-generation childe of Haqim awake at any time; should an older fourth-generation Assamite awaken, the sitting Eldest relinquishes the Black Throne after a brief transition period (typically a decade). The current Eldest is a reclusive sorcerer named Sha'hiri, who almost never leaves Alamut, governing through the leaders of the three castes.

The Caliph (warrior caste): the greatest combatant of the warriors; any subordinate may challenge him to trial by combat at any time, though the Caliph chooses the method — unarmed, armed, or military leadership. The current Caliph, Jamal, is a fierce fighter who occasionally leaves Alamut to take a direct hand in affairs in the Holy Land; clan rumor credits him with winning his position by leadership, having supposedly helped forge the Almohad Empire as his trial.

The Amr (sorcerer caste): chosen by a council of fourth- and fifth-generation sorcerers through annually repeated rituals of divination meant to identify whichever sorcerer will best serve caste and clan. Al-Ashrad, a one-eyed, one-armed wizard attended by a legion of bound demons, has held the office since being acknowledged an elder in 120 CE, confirmed anew by the divination every year since. He commands the sorcerers' spirit messengers, scrying mirrors, and djinni servants that hold the far-flung clan together.

The Vizier (vizier caste): elected every 63 years by simple majority of the vizier caste (a number the viziers refuse to explain). The current Vizier, elected in 1171, is Rebekah, an Egyptian unsurpassed in her grasp of Cainite and mortal politics, who is active on the fringes of Byzantium's courts, delighting in turning other Cainites against the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ssX4b2JFXF2uegC3]{Followers of Set}.

The Silsila: elders of the clan who no longer serve Assamite interests outside Alamut, instead acting as mentors to younger Assamites and as the clan's priesthood, keeping the vaults beneath Alamut where clay tablets from the Second City, fragments of the Book of Nod, and Haqim's first teachings are stored alongside records of the clan's support for the rise of Islam.

Source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book Two ("Saracens").

In 1102, a small cabal of warrior-caste assassins broke with the tradition of aloof siring and swift release of childer. They established a training center in Asia Minor and began taking in the most promising mortal assassins they could find, imparting to them centuries of accumulated knowledge and training in pursuit of what its founders call the "new breed of Haqim's Children." The Assamites call this shadowy brotherhood the Web of Knives; it remains dimly known to outsiders only as rumor and legend.

For seven years, students live as ghouls of the Web, bound by a loose collective blood oath to their mentors while they train in assassination and gradually learn the identities of their masters and the tenets of the Road of Blood. At the end of the seventh year the Web tests them; those who succeed receive the Embrace, and their first meal is whichever classmate failed the trial. The new Assamites then serve seven further years as field apprentices, accompanying their mentors on mercenary assassination missions. At the end of this second term, survivors undergo further testing, and those who pass diablerize those who fail.

The practice of using ghoul apprentices as prospective childer is slowly spreading through the warrior caste at large; the Caliph himself is known to have followed the Web's methodology at least once.

Source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book Two ("Saracens").

Christians are a minority within the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} clan, and those few who kept their faith after the Embrace have grown appalled at the increasingly xenophobic attitudes of the warrior caste's Muslim majority. The Spear of Destiny is a fraternal organization that crosses caste lines within the clan; membership requires only respect for the Christian faith and a desire to see the Holy Land's treasures preserved, even at the cost of the Crusades' failure.

The Spear numbers perhaps 40 Assamites in total, primarily warriors and viziers with only a handful of sorcerers, and its numbers are slowly dwindling through battlefield attrition and a decline in new European Assamites. It is currently active in Jerusalem, working to extend a treaty due to expire at the end of 1197. The warrior caste scorns the Spear's members, though many sorcerers and viziers covertly admire their dedication. The Spear is not above violence — many members were armsmen in mortal life — but has not yet stooped to assassination, instead concentrating on destroying Cainite instigators of the Crusades on both sides of the war. This has brought it into conflict with several Muslim Assamites, and some warriors in the region are considering eliminating the Spear outright.
